name: EVgo, Inc.

profile.description: EVgo, Inc. operates one of the largest public electric vehicle direct current fast charging (DCFC) networks in the United States with over 5,280 stalls across 40+ states. Services include public fast charging, eXtend (building and managing charging stations for fleet and retail partners), and OEM partnerships. Revenue split between charging network ($56M Q1 2026) and non-charging revenue ($53.8M Q1 2026). Founded in 2010, headquartered in Los Angeles, California.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): EVgo expanded its network 25% YoY to 5,280 stalls and launched NACS (Tesla-standard) connectors across 100+ stalls, opening access to the Tesla fleet [1]. Non-charging revenue surged 91% YoY to $53.8M through the eXtend platform and OEM partnerships, representing a meaningful new revenue stream beyond core charging [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI-powered products shipping or quantified AI-driven operational savings. Market Share (1/2): EVgo operates one of the largest public DCFC networks in the US but faces intense competition from Tesla Supercharger (largest US network), ChargePoint, and Electrify America; not a dominant category leader [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): 1,400-1,650 new stalls planned for 2026 with majority in H2, and DOE loan facility amended to $750M capacity providing capital for expansion [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): As a charging infrastructure operator, R&D spending is modest relative to technology peers; no R&D figures disclosed.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): EVgo's mission to 'accelerate the mass adoption of electric vehicles by building a convenient, reliable fast-charging network while eliminating emissions to protect our planet' is specific, purpose-driven, and directly ties commercial activity to environmental impact [5]. The mission has guided decisions to match 100% of electricity with renewable energy credits and prioritize network accessibility. Community Impact (1/2): EVgo purchases renewable energy credits for 100% of network consumption and maintains sustainability commitments across operations, though no specific dollar amounts for community programs or charitable giving were identified [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor reviews reveal mixed signals including two rounds of layoffs, cultural concerns, and management criticism alongside some positive reviews citing mission-driven culture [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Badar Khan sold $117K of EVGO stock in March 2026, and insiders have collectively sold $1.5M more than they bought in the last 12 months [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Q1 2026 delivered record revenue of $109.5M (+45% YoY) with GAAP gross margin of 11.8% and adjusted gross margin of 27.1% [1]. The company remains deeply unprofitable with net loss of $37.0M and operating loss of $36.4M in Q1 2026, reflecting the capital-intensive buildout phase [1]. D/E of 91% is manageable given the $750M DOE loan facility, with $122.4M cash against $211.5M total debt [1]. ROE of -27.4% and profit margin of -11.1% reflect pre-profitability status, though adjusted EBITDA guidance of $(20)M to $20M for FY2026 suggests a path toward breakeven [1][2]. Revenue growth of 45% YoY is strong, supported by the 17th consecutive quarter of double-digit charging revenue growth [1].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): EVgo's core business is building, owning, and operating physical EV charging infrastructure — stations, power equipment, land leases, and grid interconnections that AI structurally cannot displace [1]. The physical act of delivering electricity to vehicles through hardware requires real-world construction, permitting, and utility coordination far beyond AI's reach. Rising AI data center buildout increases total electricity demand and grid investment, indirectly supporting charging infrastructure economics. The only minor exposure is in software-layer competition where AI-optimized routing or dynamic pricing from competitors could modestly affect utilization rates. AI Opportunity (0/1): No evidence of AI-powered products generating quantifiable revenue. EVgo uses standard fleet management and network monitoring tools but has not deployed AI products or reported AI-driven savings.

infinite_game.summary: EVgo demonstrates genuine environmental purpose and willingness to invest through sustained losses, but cultural concerns from employee reviews, recent leadership transition, and a short operating history as a public company prevent a higher score. The mission is authentic and guides strategic decisions, but hasn't been tested across major market cycles or leadership transitions.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): EVgo's purpose of accelerating EV adoption to eliminate emissions connects commercial activity to a meaningful environmental cause that existed before the company and will outlast any single product [5]. The mission guided the decision to match 100% of electricity with renewable energy credits and to prioritize network accessibility. However, EVgo has not yet been tested through a major market crisis or leadership transition — CEO Badar Khan was appointed only in November 2023 [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor reviews reveal concerning patterns including two rounds of layoffs, allegations of cultural issues including harassment, criticism of management as 'out of touch,' and descriptions of the company as 'horribly mismanaged' and 'directionless' [3]. While some positive reviews cite good teammates and mission-driven culture, the negative signals — particularly regarding psychological safety — indicate a low-trust environment by Sinek's standards.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): EVgo's adoption of NACS connectors (Tesla's charging standard) across 100+ stalls demonstrates willingness to learn from a rival's strength rather than clinging to CCS exclusivity [1]. The decision to embrace a competitor's technology standard because it serves EV drivers better reflects an infinite competitive mindset — improving the product based on what rivals do well rather than defending proprietary territory.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): EVgo has evolved from a pure public charging operator to a multi-revenue platform, adding the eXtend business and OEM partnerships that now represent 49% of total revenue ($53.8M non-charging vs $56M charging in Q1 2026) [1]. This revenue diversification shows meaningful strategic adaptation, though it is incremental rather than a transformative business model pivot.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): EVgo continues to invest aggressively despite persistent losses, spending $30.6M in capital expenditures in Q1 2026 (+104% YoY) and securing a $750M DOE loan facility for network expansion [1]. The company prioritizes long-term infrastructure buildout over near-term profitability, with GAAP operating cash flow of -$35.4M in Q1. This willingness to invest through losses for long-term positioning shows courage, though the strategy is partly enabled by government funding rather than purely management conviction.

investment_thesis: EVgo delivered record Q1 2026 revenue of $109.5M (+45% YoY) driven by 18% charging network growth and 91% non-charging revenue expansion through the eXtend platform [1]. The company affirmed FY2026 guidance of $410-$470M revenue with adjusted EBITDA of $(20)M to $20M, suggesting a path toward breakeven [1]. With 5,280 stalls (+25% YoY), 1.7M customer accounts, and a $750M DOE loan facility, EVgo has the capital and scale to capture the accelerating EV adoption curve. The NACS connector rollout expands the addressable market to Tesla's fleet, and 1,400-1,650 new stalls planned for 2026 will extend network coverage into underserved corridors [1].
thesis_continued: The primary concern is persistent unprofitability and cash burn — net loss of $37.0M and operating cash outflow of $35.4M in Q1 alone, with only $122.4M cash on hand [1]. At $1.91 per share (down 52% over 52 weeks), the $609M market cap prices in significant execution risk [4]. Adjusted gross margin declined 660 basis points YoY to 27.1% as lower-margin non-charging revenue grew faster than charging revenue [1]. Competition from Tesla Supercharger's expanding third-party access, ChargePoint, and Electrify America intensifies pricing pressure. Employee culture concerns including layoffs and workplace conduct allegations create organizational risk during a critical scaling phase [3]. The company's trajectory depends on reaching EBITDA breakeven before its cash runway expires.
key_catalysts: Achievement of adjusted EBITDA breakeven in FY2026 at the high end of guidance ($20M), which would validate the business model's unit economics as the network scales beyond 6,500 stalls
NACS connector rollout across the full network unlocking the Tesla fleet as new customers, potentially accelerating throughput per stall from the current 91 GWh quarterly run-rate
Conversion of the $750M DOE loan facility into deployed stalls at accelerated pace in H2 2026, with 1,400-1,650 new stalls doubling the construction rate versus prior years
key_risks: Cash burn of $35.4M per quarter against $122.4M cash reserves creates a constrained runway without additional DOE loan drawdowns, with net loss widening 41% YoY in Q1 2026
Tesla Supercharger's expansion to third-party vehicles and potential NEVI funding eligibility threatens EVgo's competitive position as the largest non-Tesla public DCFC network
Glassdoor reviews citing layoffs, cultural issues, and management concerns during a critical scaling phase risk employee attrition and execution failures when the company can least afford disruption
